# Welcome to Speech Processing! {.unnumbered}

![](/images/gy_chili.png){ width=15% style="float:right; padding:10px" }

::: {.callout-tip}
## What You'll Learn

By the end of this tutorial, you will be able to:

- Load and inspect `.wav` audio files in R  
- Visualize waveforms and spectrograms  
- Split audio into smaller chunks  
- Perform automatic speech recognition (ASR) using Whisper  
- Extract time-aligned transcription information  
- Perform forced alignment (conceptually and practically)  
- Extract acoustic features such as vowel formants  
- Visualize vowel space (F1–F2 plots)  
- Combine acoustic and lexical information for linguistic analysis  
:::

---

## What Is Speech Processing?

**Speech processing** refers to computational methods for analyzing spoken language.  

Instead of starting with text, we begin with **raw acoustic signals** and extract:

- Linguistic structure (words, segments)
- Temporal alignment
- Acoustic features (formants, pitch, intensity)
- Speaker characteristics

---

## Why Speech Processing Matters

### Linguistic Applications

| Research Area | Application |
|--------------|------------|
| **Phonetics** | Measure vowel formants |
| **Sociophonetics** | Compare speakers or groups |
| **Prosody research** | Extract pitch and intensity |
| **Corpus linguistics** | Align speech with transcripts |
| **Forensic linguistics** | Speaker identification |
| **Language acquisition** | Analyze pronunciation development |

### From Signal to Structure

Speech processing typically follows this pipeline:

```
Audio (.wav)
   ↓
Segmentation
   ↓
Automatic Speech Recognition
   ↓
Forced Alignment
   ↓
Feature Extraction
   ↓
Statistical Analysis
```

# 1. Setup

## Install and Load Required Packages

```{r}
# install.packages(c("tuneR", "seewave", "reticulate", "dplyr", "ggplot2"))

library(tuneR)
library(seewave)
library(reticulate)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

---

# 2. Loading and Inspecting Audio

## Load a WAV File

The wav file is taken from https://doi.org/10.17866/rd.salford.7857770

```{r}
audio_path <- here::here("tutorials/speechprocessing/data/sample.wav")

wav <- readWave(audio_path)

wav
```

## Basic Properties

```{r}
duration <- length(wav@left) / wav@samp.rate
sampling_rate <- wav@samp.rate

duration
sampling_rate
```

---

# 3. Visualizing the Signal

## Waveform

```{r}
plot(wav, main = "Waveform")
```

## Spectrogram

```{r}
spectro(wav, main = "Spectrogram")
```

Waveforms show amplitude over time.  
Spectrograms show frequency over time.

---

# 4. Splitting Audio into Chunks

Segment long recordings into smaller units.

```{r}
chunk_length <- 5  # seconds
samples_per_chunk <- chunk_length * wav@samp.rate

total_samples <- length(wav@left)
n_chunks <- ceiling(total_samples / samples_per_chunk)

chunks <- list()

for (i in 1:n_chunks) {
  start <- ((i - 1) * samples_per_chunk) + 1
  end <- min(i * samples_per_chunk, total_samples)
  chunks[[i]] <- extractWave(wav, from = start, to = end, xunit = "samples")
}

length(chunks)
```

---

# 5. Automatic Speech Recognition (Whisper)

Whisper is a neural speech recognition model.

### Install Whisper (Python)

```bash
pip install openai-whisper
```

### Load Whisper via reticulate

```{r eval = F}
whisper <- import("whisper")
model <- whisper$load_model("base")
```

### Transcribe Audio

```{r eval = F}
result <- model$transcribe(audio_path)

transcript <- result$text
transcript
```

### Extract Time-Aligned Segments

```{r eval = F}
segments <- result$segments

alignment_df <- data.frame(
  start = sapply(segments, function(x) x$start),
  end   = sapply(segments, function(x) x$end),
  text  = sapply(segments, function(x) x$text)
)

alignment_df
```

---

# 6. Forced Alignment

**Forced alignment** links words or phonemes to precise time stamps.

Options:

- Montreal Forced Aligner (external tool)
- Whisper segment timestamps (approximate alignment)

Alignment allows us to connect:

> Text ↔ Time ↔ Acoustic Signal

---

# 7. Extracting Acoustic Features

## Vowel Formants

Formants (F1, F2, F3) represent resonant frequencies of the vocal tract.

```{r eval = F}
formants <- formant(wav, fmax = 5000, plot = FALSE)

formant_df <- data.frame(
  time = formants[,1],
  F1 = formants[,2],
  F2 = formants[,3]
)

head(formant_df)
```

---

# 8. Visualizing Vowel Space

```{r eval = F}
ggplot(formant_df, aes(x = F2, y = F1)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  scale_y_reverse() +
  scale_x_reverse() +
  labs(title = "Vowel Space (F1–F2)",
       x = "F2 (Hz)",
       y = "F1 (Hz)")
```

Reversing axes follows phonetic convention.

---

# 9. Linking Alignment and Acoustics

We can extract formants only during specific words.

```{r eval = F}
first_segment <- alignment_df[1, ]

subset_formants <- formant_df %>%
  filter(time >= first_segment$start,
         time <= first_segment$end)

head(subset_formants)
```

This enables:

- Word-specific acoustic analysis  
- Sociophonetic comparisons  
- Phoneme-level modeling  

---

In this tutorial, you learned how to:

Speech processing connects:

> Raw Signal → Linguistic Structure → Quantitative Features
